A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ToDi and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The comparison accounts for material moved from v1’s appendices into v2’s main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original distillation experiments, ROUGE-L results, GPT-4o preference evaluations, and ablation analyses, including additional-model results in Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, preference evaluations, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The token-wise FKL/RKL mixture, sigmoid log-ratio weighting, stop-gradient operation, and generalized β formulation remain unchanged in Equations 7–11. No algorithmic component or training objective is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use Dolly training data and evaluate instruction following on DollyEval, S-NI, UnNI, SelfInst, and VicunaEval. Moving additional-model results into the main text introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain SFT, FKL, RKL, JS, TVD, SKL, SRKL, and AKL. DistiLLM-2 is newly discussed as related work but is not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported splits, model configurations, training budgets, ROUGE-L evaluation, and pairwise judging procedures are unchanged. OLMo2, Qwen2.5, and Gemma3 configurations in v2 already appeared in v1 Appendix E.

E4.justification: The toy example, convergence analysis, β ablations, fixed-mixture comparisons, and Pearson-similarity analysis are retained. V1 Appendix G’s sensitivity study becomes part of v2 Section 5.3 without changing its tested settings or evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five evaluation seeds, with Appendix D listing {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}. The ± reporting, plotted uncertainty, and preference-evaluation p-values are unchanged; no new statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. Table 3 retains ToDi averages of 18.66 and 24.83; v2 Table 4 combines existing DollyEval entries from v1 Tables 3 and 6. Sensitivity scores and Pearson similarities are likewise retained.

T1.justification: The gradient analysis, weighting conditions, generalized formulation, and Appendix A–C derivations are unchanged. Mathematical differences are limited to spacing and typesetting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about complementary gradients, token-wise divergence control, empirical superiority, and efficiency. Relocated evidence does not broaden these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of weighting, convergence, distribution alignment, and β sensitivity are retained. Both versions state the same limitations concerning shared vocabularies, access to teacher probabilities, and untested extremely large models.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract footnote. Appendix D’s hardware, hyperparameters, loss mixture, and data-processing details remain unchanged. The GPT-4o caption clarification identifies the judge already specified in v1 Appendix F.

R1.justification: V2 adds a brief discussion and citation of Ko et al. (2025), DistiLLM-2, and removes Minka et al. (2005). Other reference changes mainly update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate entries, without substantially revising ToDi’s positioning.

P1.justification: V1’s additional-model and sensitivity appendices are integrated into Sections 5.2 and 5.3, with corresponding heading and cross-reference edits. V2 also makes limited wording changes and expands acknowledgments; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 presents the additional-model table in the main text with two columns of previously reported DollyEval results, relocates the sensitivity table, and adjusts figure/table placement. Figure graphics are unchanged, while Figure 7’s caption is clarified to GPT-4o.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves documentation and accessibility by adding a code-availability link, integrating existing model comparisons and sensitivity evidence into the main discussion, and updating related work. The method, theory, protocols, and empirical findings remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
